title: Compact atom-free H^(1/2) holonomy counterexample and endpoint replacement

endpoint_boundary.density: epsilon_n=e^(-n), w_n=1/[n(n+1)], tau_epsilon(x)=epsilon^(-1)(1-|x|/epsilon)_+, and f=sum_(n>=1)w_n tau_(epsilon_n) is a compact L1 probability density.
endpoint_boundary.positive_transform: mu=f dx is atom-free and widehat mu(t)=sum_(n>=1)w_n sinc^2(epsilon_n t/2)>=0.
endpoint_boundary.primitive: For F(x)=mu((-infinity,x]) and G(x)=F(x)-F(x-1), G is nonnegative, compact, AC and BV, DG=[f(x)-f(x-1)]dx, and it widehat G(t)=(1-e^(-it))widehat mu(t).
endpoint_boundary.endpoint_result: sum_n int_(I_n)t|widehat G(t)|^2dt<infinity but sum_n int_(I_n)|widehat G(t)|dt=infinity, so G belongs to H^(1/2) while widehat G does not belong to L1.
endpoint_boundary.k1628_compatibility: The multiscale density f is not in L2, so the example does not contradict K1628.
endpoint_boundary.endpoint_sufficient: Low-frequency L2 plus sum_j[int_(A_j)|t||widehat G(t)|^2dt]^(1/2)<infinity on dyadic annuli implies widehat G in L1 by shellwise Cauchy-Schwarz.
endpoint_boundary.scope_guard: The Besov-type endpoint condition is sufficient, not necessary, and no electric-field L1, nonlinear remainder, or source-owned flow follows.
